concepts.def: Transmission Control Protocol: reliable, connection-oriented delivery with retransmission of lost packets.
Internet Protocol: addresses and routes packets between hosts across networks.
Hypertext Transfer Protocol: client-server protocol used by web browsers to fetch web pages.
HTTP secured by TLS, encrypting traffic to protect against eavesdropping.
File Transfer Protocol: moves files between computers across a network.
Simple Mail Transfer Protocol: used to send email between servers.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Internet & Its Uses — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Internet & Its Uses brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Internet & Its Uses.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
